description.p: OpenSSL Encrypt is a comprehensive encryption tool that provides military-grade security with cutting-edge post-quantum cryptography. Protect your files against both current and future quantum computing threats.

ul.li: Multiple symmetric encryption algorithms (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, Fernet, etc.)
Post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM, HQC, Kyber) for quantum-resistant protection
Advanced password protection with multiple KDF options (Argon2, Scrypt)
Secure file operations with secure deletion

description.p: Perfect for individuals and organizations requiring the highest levels of data protection, including protection against future quantum computer attacks.
To report bugs or request features, send email to: issue+world-openssl-encrypt-2-issue-+gitlab@rm-rf.ch

NOT YET RELEASED (in development). Security hardening: DERIVE-PASSWORD MEMORY HYGIENE (2026-07-13): the derive-password command now zeroizes the hardware pepper and the derived-key output buffer after use instead of leaving them in process memory (derived outputs unchanged). LEGACY SEED ZEROIZATION (2026-07-13): key derivation for legacy sequential formats now builds its password+salt+pepper seed in a wipeable buffer that is zeroized after use (derived keys are byte-identical). BALLOON V14 FAIL-CLOSED (2026-07-13): version-14 files whose balloon KDF metadata is missing the space_cost field are refused with a clear error instead of silently deriving with a weak fallback; older files (where the fallback is required for compatibility) are unaffected. KDF COST MEMORY CEILING (2026-07-24): decryption now refuses a crafted file or keystore whose key-derivation cost parameters (Argon2 memory, scrypt N, balloon space_cost) would exhaust memory — previously an attacker-supplied file could drive a multi-terabyte allocation and crash the host on decrypt before any password check. Peak memory is estimated before key derivation runs and refused above an 8 GiB safety ceiling (four times the largest built-in preset, so no legitimate file is affected), overridable per file with --allow-high-kdf-cost or an interactive confirmation. Only memory is hard-guarded; CPU/time cost stays advisory. IDENTITY-FILE KDF COST BOUND (2026-07-24, gitlab#129): identity unlock now clamps the Argon2 cost parameters read from an identity file to sane maxima before deriving the key — a tampered or attacker-authored identity with a gigabyte-scale memory_cost could otherwise OOM the host on unlock before authentication. Legitimate identities use the 64 MB default and are unaffected. PLUGIN SIGNATURE ENFORCE-BY-DEFAULT (2026-07-24, gitlab#130): the plugin loader now refuses an unsigned or unverifiable third-party plugin by default instead of running it behind a bypassable code scan — loading arbitrary plugin code was effectively arbitrary code execution for anyone who could place a file in a plugin directory. A non-built-in plugin must now carry a valid signature from an enrolled trust anchor, or it is refused before its code runs; built-in bundled plugins are unaffected, so no shipped functionality changes. Users who intentionally load unsigned third-party plugins can opt back in via the OPENSSL_ENCRYPT_PLUGIN_SIGNATURE_POLICY=warn (or off) environment variable. The built-in trust shortcut is now scoped to the shipped plugin subtree, so the third-party plugin directories (user/community/official) are no longer auto-trusted and must carry a valid signature. PQC KEYFILE ARGON2ID WRAP (2026-07-24, gitlab#131): a .pqc keyfile created with --pqc-keyfile wrapped the long-lived post-quantum private key with a weak PBKDF2-SHA256 100k key, so an attacker who obtained the keyfile could brute-force the wrapping password cheaply offline. New keyfiles now wrap the private key with Argon2id (consistent with the rest of the tool); existing keyfiles still decrypt unchanged. Re-save or regenerate a keyfile to move it onto the stronger wrapping. DUAL-ENCRYPTION VERIFIER (2026-07-24, gitlab#131): dual-encrypted files stored a weak 10k-PBKDF2 file-password verifier in cleartext metadata that an attacker with the file could brute-force offline. It is no longer used or written; the file password is authenticated by the keystore's dual-encryption AES-GCM tag instead, and a mismatched file/keystore dual-encryption state now fails closed. Legacy files still decrypt unchanged; re-encrypt them to drop the weak verifier. PORTABLE-USB INTEGRITY (2026-07-24, gitlab#132): integrity verification of a portable USB drive did not detect files added to the drive, including a root-level autorun payload auto-executed by the OS. New drives now record an allowlist of every file in the tool tree (plus the root autorun files) and flag ANY file added afterward — a planted library or any other payload, not just a fixed set of file types (the user's encrypt/decrypt workspace is excluded, so normal use still verifies); older drives verify as before, re-create a drive for the stronger checks. The hash-manifest fallback also now uses the drive's unique per-drive salt. LOW SECURITY FIXES (2026-07-24, gitlab#133-136): the plugin sandbox no longer authorizes a sibling plugin directory that shares a name prefix (a sandboxed plugin could reach another plugin's data); the keyserver bearer token passed to 'keyserver set-token' is now redacted in the --debug output (rotate any token previously used with --debug); trust-anchor enrollment now requires the full key fingerprint instead of accepting a forgeable short key id; and the PIV smartcard PIN is handled with one fewer non-wipeable in-memory copy. Desktop GUI: the Decrypt tab can now decrypt files encrypted to an identity — its Advanced Options expose a decryption-identity selector and, once an identity is chosen, controls to verify the sender signature or (with an explicit off-by-default warning) skip signature verification. New Password Generator screen produces passwords via the CLI in both character mode (length and character-class toggles) and diceware passphrase mode (word count, separator, optional wordlist), showing entropy/strength with copy-to-clipboard. New Secure Shred screen securely overwrites and deletes files/directories via the CLI with a selectable pass count and recursive toggle, behind a mandatory irreversible-action confirmation. The Encrypt tab gains a live password-strength meter (bar, category, entropy, weakness warnings) driven by the CLI check-password command. New Rekey screen re-encrypts an existing file with a new password (and optionally a new algorithm) via the CLI rekey command, passing passwords through environment variables the CLI clears after reading. RECOVERY CREDENTIALS VIA ENVIRONMENT (2026-07-25, gitlab#144): recovery codes could previously be passed only on the command line, where they are visible in the process list and carried no warning, and recovery passphrases only through an interactive terminal prompt — so scripts and the desktop GUI could not use them safely or at all. Recovery codes and passphrases can now be supplied through dedicated environment variables that the CLI reads once and clears immediately, and passing a recovery code on the command line now warns that it is visible in the process list. The primary file password supplied through CRYPT_PASSWORD is cleared the same way on these commands. An explicit command-line flag still chooses which credential is used, so a stray or planted environment variable cannot silently add a recovery passphrase to a file, and a blank value is refused rather than leaving the tool waiting at a prompt. DESKTOP GUI RECOVERY SLOTS (2026-07-25, gitlab#145): the desktop app gains a Recovery screen that lists a file's recovery slots, adds a recovery code or passphrase, removes a slot behind an explicit confirmation, and decrypts a file with a recovery credential when the password is unavailable. A newly generated recovery code is shown once and never written to a log. The app also no longer records a command's standard output in its debug log by default, since that output can contain decrypted content or a newly generated credential. RECOVERY COMMANDS MACHINE-READABLE OUTPUT (2026-07-25, gitlab#146): the recovery-slot commands gain a --json option so scripts and the desktop app can read a file's recovery slots without parsing human-readable text, and the report now says which credential produced a newly added slot. A newly generated recovery code is never printed to the output or message streams in this mode: it unlocks the file, so the tool writes it to a file of your choosing that only you can read, and the report contains just the path. GLOBAL OPTIONS AFTER A COMMAND (2026-07-25, gitlab#171): options such as --debug, --verbose and --quiet were rejected when written after a command name for roughly half the commands, including identity, keyserver, telemetry, plugin and the recovery commands, so the desktop app's debug toggle made those commands fail outright. They are now accepted after any command. Where a command has its own --quiet, the value is no longer silently discarded. GUI CONTACT IMPORT (2026-07-25, gitlab#164): importing a contact from the desktop app never worked - the app sent options the command line did not accept, so every import failed immediately. The import command now reads a contact document from standard input and accepts a local alias for the contact. The document is deliberately not accepted as a command-line value, since the command line is readable by other users on the machine and the field is a free-text paste box. KEYSERVER LOGIN REDACTION (2026-07-25, gitlab#171): the keyserver login identifier is a credential and is now hidden in --debug output and in logs, and third-party network libraries no longer log full request addresses under --debug, which could contain a contact's email address. Neither could occur in a released version, because --debug was previously rejected for those commands. SECOND PASSWORD AND SIGNER PASSPHRASE VIA ENVIRONMENT (2026-07-25, gitlab#154/#159): the second password for keyed hidden mode and the signing passphrase for the sign command could previously be entered only at an interactive terminal prompt, so scripts and the desktop app could not use those features at all. OPENSSL_ENCRYPT_SECOND_PASSWORD and OPENSSL_ENCRYPT_SIGNER_PASSPHRASE now supply them; each is read once and cleared immediately, a blank value is refused rather than leaving the tool waiting at a prompt, and neither variable can switch a feature on by itself - hidden mode still needs its option, and an identity protected only by hardware is never asked for a passphrase. IDENTITY DISPLAY SANITIZATION (2026-08-07, gitlab#172): the email field of an imported contact document was printed to the terminal unchecked, directly above the fingerprint line used for out-of-band verification, so a malicious contact file could embed terminal control sequences that overwrite the displayed fingerprint with one the victim trusts. The same gap existed on the keyserver trust prompt — which displays a key bundle fetched from a remote server, an even stronger attack position — on stored identity files read back from disk, on several signature-file fields (including one printed inside the GOOD-signature verdict even though it is not covered by the signature), and in keyserver error messages that echoed a raw server response. Contact metadata (email, fingerprint, creation date) is now validated everywhere it enters the program (import, create, load from disk, keyserver bundle, signature sidecar), and every terminal display of it — including data imported or cached by earlier versions — escapes control characters instead of printing them, as do the error messages that echo a rejected name or alias. GUI IDENTITY LISTING (2026-08-07, gitlab#183): the desktop app's identity list was always empty - it asked the command line for machine-readable output using an option that did not exist, so every listing failed silently. The option now exists, and the app's Identity Management screen, Decrypt tab identity selector and main window list identities again. Contact details shown in the app also neutralize invisible text-direction characters, which could otherwise make an address render reversed. The app also reports store entries it could not load instead of leaving them out of the list silently, and an identity list that fails now shows an error instead of an empty list. IDENTITY NAME COLLISION (2026-08-07, gitlab#173): a contact could be stored under the same name as one of your own identities. The contact stayed hidden while your identity existed, but deleting that identity handed the name - and any file you later encrypted to it - to the contact's keys. Such a name is now refused outright, deleting a name removes both entries, and any collision already on disk is reported by 'identity list'. Deleting such a name now asks which entry to remove and shows both fingerprints first, since removing your own identity destroys its private keys; the name 'contacts' is also reserved, as an entry stored under it was hidden from the listing yet still usable. ENVELOPE REWRITE DATA LOSS (2026-08-07): adding or removing a recovery slot, and rekeying an envelope file, could rewrite the file by truncating it — a crash, power loss or full disk part-way through left a shortened, unreadable file and no copy of the original, which for a same-file rewrite is the user's only ciphertext. The rewrite is now atomic (written to a temporary file in the same directory, flushed to disk, then renamed over the original with its permissions preserved), and where a rename cannot be used — a symlink, or a file with more than one hard link, both of which must be written through to stay consistent — the original is copied to a backup first and restored if the write fails. POST-QUANTUM KEYFILE (2026-08-08): the --pqc-keyfile option could never actually save a key: the option that triggers saving was not accepted by the encrypt command at all, so pointing --pqc-keyfile at a new path was silently ignored — you got a one-off key, no file, and no way to open the file again with the keyfile you thought you had created. It now works, refuses a missing keyfile with a clear instruction instead of ignoring it, and writes the key file readable only by you. A second, older copy of this code that stored the post-quantum private key unencrypted has been removed. SEVEN COMMANDS COULD NOT BE RUN (2026-08-08): create-usb, verify-usb, list-plugins, plugin-info, enable-plugin, disable-plugin and reload-plugin were listed in the help output and documented, but every one of them failed immediately with 'invalid choice' — the whole portable-USB and plugin-management command surface was unreachable. They now run. PEPPER MANAGEMENT COMMANDS (2026-08-09, gitlab#193): the remote-pepper server had working operations but no command-line access, so the desktop app's pepper controls failed silently. A new 'plugin pepper' command group adds them — list stored peppers, test the connection, set up and verify TOTP two-factor authentication, and configure the pepper dead-man's switch. The two-factor secret and one-time backup codes are printed only to standard output (never to the log the app keeps) and are redacted from debug output. The dead-man's switch, which erases every pepper if you miss a check-in, now refuses an interval shorter than one day so it can never be armed with an already-past deadline. FILE-INTEGRITY VERIFICATION COMMANDS (2026-08-09, gitlab#194): the remote file-integrity service likewise had no command-line access, so the app's integrity controls could not reach it. A new 'plugin integrity' command group adds a connection test, verification statistics, and per-file verification. Verification deliberately reports four distinct outcomes — match, mismatch, file-not-registered, and service-unreachable — so a file the service has never seen, or a service that cannot be reached, is never mistaken for a tampered file (the mistake the removed app feature made). ONLYKEY IDENTITY WRONG-DEVICE BINDING (2026-08-09, gitlab#218, security advisory 2026-18, Medium): creating an identity with 'identity create --hsm onlykey' silently bound it to a YubiKey instead of the OnlyKey — the selected device was used only for an availability pre-check and never for the actual key protection, which always defaulted to the YubiKey plugin. With only an OnlyKey attached, creation failed with a misleading 'no Yubikey available' error; with both devices attached, the identity was gated by the YubiKey and could never be opened with the OnlyKey. The selected device is now threaded through identity creation and the private-key encrypt/decrypt paths, so an OnlyKey identity uses the OnlyKey end to end, and the error messages name the configured device. Existing YubiKey identities are unaffected. If you created an OnlyKey identity on an earlier release with both devices attached, re-create it on this release to bind it to the OnlyKey. TELEMETRY OPT-OUT NOW STICKS (2026-08-09, gitlab#166): opting out of the optional anonymous telemetry stopped uploads and deleted the stored key but wrote no persistent off-switch, so a telemetry-enabling environment variable that was still set silently turned collection back on and registered a fresh key the next time you ran the tool. Opting out now writes a persistent marker that keeps telemetry off regardless of that environment variable until you remove the marker. MACHINE-READABLE SECURITY ANALYSIS (2026-08-09, gitlab#162): the analyze-security and smart-recommendations commands gain --output-format json, and telemetry status gains --json, each printing its result as JSON so the desktop app reads the real security readout and telemetry state instead of guessing from human-readable text; the JSON carries only algorithm settings, scores and advice, never secrets.

New check-password command reports password strength (pattern-aware category, entropy, weakness warnings, and pass/fail against a chosen policy) without encrypting anything, with --json for scripting. Pattern-aware password strength estimation now flags predictable structure (dictionary words, l33t substitutions, keyboard walks, sequences, repeats, dates) with an advisory-by-default label and an optional --strict-strength gate; it affects encryption-time validation only, never decryption. The loud --debug data-logging banner now fires only for --debug --unsafe-show-secrets (the cleartext path), while plain --debug (which redacts secrets) shows a calm, accurate note. SECURITY REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (2026-07-07): removed an unconditional cleartext print of the derived FIDO2/HSM hardware pepper (H1); the plugin loader now verifies, hash-pins, AST-scans and executes the exact same bytes, closing a verify-one-copy/execute-another gap and a .pyc shadow (M1); package plugins are now covered by a signed per-package PLUGIN.manifest over every importable module, so a signed __init__.py plus a tampered sibling is refused under enforce (H2); several no-op secure_memzero call sites that wiped a throwaway copy now wipe the real secret (M2); the parallel and sequential Independent-XOR paths derive identical keys for Argon2 multi-round configs (M3) and RandomX now fails closed in the parallel path (R1); and streaming per-chunk AEAD authentication failures are classified structurally instead of by error-string matching (M4). Earlier hardening (audit 2026-07-06): per-round KDF debug lines no longer leak a derived-key intermediate by default, and new files are no longer written in the cost-bypassing v8/v10 sequential-XOR format (encrypt now defaults to format version 9 and refuses new v8/v10, while existing v8/v10 files still decrypt and rekey upgrades them). Also fixes string_entropy Unicode handling. CROSS-LINE PQC KEM COMPATIBILITY (2026-07-10): PQC KEM keys for format version 12+ files are now derived with HKDF-SHA256 matching the 1.5.x line, so v12/v13 PQC files interoperate across maintenance lines; files written by releases up to 1.4.7 with the legacy derivation remain fully decryptable via an authenticated legacy retry with a re-encryption notice. Also fixes decryption of v11-v13 files carrying an embedded password-encrypted post-quantum private key (previously always failed with a missing-salt error). FORMAT VERSION 14 GROUNDWORK (not yet the default): new independent-XOR-only format with a length-prefixed KDF seed — password, salt and hardware pepper enter key derivation as unambiguous length-prefixed fields instead of raw concatenation — plus fail-closed version guards; v14 PQC files additionally bind the KEM symmetric key to the full transcript (algorithm, AEAD choice and encapsulation ciphertext); all files below v14 derive byte-identically to before. FORMAT VERSION 14 IS NOW THE DEFAULT WRITE FORMAT: new encryptions (including streaming) default to the independent-XOR robust-combiner key derivation, wide keys derive at full length, sequential XOR stays available as a v13-pinned opt-in, and every existing file decrypts unchanged. Also fixes a data-loss bug where sequential XOR combined with streaming wrote files that could never be decrypted (now refused with a clear error), keystore dual-encryption failing for files at format versions 11-13, and a key-derivation crash when RandomX was combined with wide-key ciphers (AES-SIV, Threefish). POST-V14 REVIEW HARDENING (2026-07-11): the v14 KDF seed encoder now writes into a single exact-size buffer, so no partial copies of secret material can be left behind in unwiped reallocated memory (derived keys and the on-disk format are byte-identical); keystore metadata version checks now reject malformed version fields with a clean error instead of crashing on crafted files (valid files are unaffected); and recipient (asymmetric) files now bind the post-quantum key-encapsulation ciphertext and algorithm into the password-wrap key derivation (defense-in-depth transcript binding, wrap_version 3) — every existing file keeps decrypting, but recipient files written from this version on cannot be opened by older releases. Fully backward-compatible decryption of files made with supported algorithms. V14 FOLLOW-UP HARDENING (2026-07-11): remote and combined KDF pepper material is now held in wipeable buffers and zeroized after use on the encrypt and decrypt paths (previously immutable copies could linger in memory until garbage collection; no derived keys or file formats change). Encrypting with an unknown future format_version is now refused up front instead of writing a permanently unreadable file. Legacy (pre-1.4.8) post-quantum files using XChaCha20-Poly1305 now decrypt via the intended legacy-key retry, and structural decode errors are no longer misreported as authentication failures. HSM TEST-COMMAND HARDENING (2026-07-12): the earlier H1 pepper-print fix had landed in a CLI frontend that is not actually dispatched — the live hsm fido2-test and onlykey-test handlers now report only the pepper length instead of hex-dumping the derived hardware pepper, the FIDO2 pepper plugin no longer includes raw prf/hmac-secret output in debug logs or error messages, and the module self-test prints lengths instead of test-secret hex; regression tests now cover the live code paths.

Documentation and packaging release: refreshes the project page and README (rendered as the PyPI page) for the 1.4.6 feature set, including the key-derivation documentation, which now reflects format version 13 as the Independent XOR default. No functional, CLI, or on-disk format changes.

New PIV / PKCS#11 HSM backend (--hsm piv) that derives the key-derivation pepper from a PIV private key on a smart card, and source-code integrity protection (verify-integrity) backed by a PGP-signed SHA-512 manifest. New ASCII armor output (encrypt --armor) writes paste-safe PEM-style Base64 with CRC-24 truncation detection, auto-detected on decrypt. Encrypt-to-self now adds the sender as a recipient by default so senders can decrypt their own outbound files (opt out with --no-encrypt-to-self). New detached post-quantum file signing (sign / verify-signature with ML-DSA-65) adds authenticity that symmetric AEAD alone cannot provide. New opt-in envelope encryption (--envelope) encrypts data under a random key wrapped by the password, enabling fast credential rekey (rewrap the key instead of re-encrypting the file) and a foundation for multi-password access; for a cascade chain the wrap uses the same chain so it is never the weak link. Independent XOR key derivation now uses per-component domain-separated salts (format version 13) by default. This release also fixes a key-derivation cost bypass in the optional, non-default sequential XOR mode, disclosed as security advisory GHSA-vxf9-vwp6-2w43; default configurations were unaffected and existing files remain decryptable.

Security dependency update: urllib3 2.7.0, cryptography 46.0.7, pillow 12.2.0, idna 3.15 — fixes for CVE-2026-44431/44432, CVE-2026-39892, a PSD decoder out-of-bounds write, and an idna DoS. New CI check keeps flatpak dependency pins aligned with the package requirements.

Security hardening release: authenticated keystore format, D-Bus polkit authorization, fail-closed PQC algorithm resolution, plugin sandbox enforcement, per-drive USB salts. New: cross-device YubiKey/OnlyKey HSM decryption, encrypt-CLI reconstruction from file metadata via the info action, Diceware passphrase generation, HSM-aware derive-password. Threefish extension builds on Python 3.14. Requires Python 3.11+.
Fix Flutter GUI launcher in Flatpak: corrected binary name so --gui flag works correctly.

Desktop GUI Simple/Pro mode toggle — Simple mode (default) hides all advanced options and uses the modernized STANDARD template. New defaults: SHA3-512 + BLAKE3 hashes, RandomX + Argon2 KDFs, cascade encryption (AES-256-GCM + ChaCha20-Poly1305), Independent XOR (v11) key derivation. Dependency bumps: cryptography 46.0.6, requests 2.33.0, black 26.3.1, nltk 3.9.4.

Streaming chunked AEAD encryption (format v12) for constant-memory large file handling, full Windows compatibility, stderr output separation, comprehensive security hardening, and dependency security updates.
Security dependency update: bumped nltk to 3.9.3 (CVE-2026-33236, CVE-2026-33231, CVE-2026-33230, GHSA-rf74-v2fm-23pw).
Streaming chunked encryption (format v12), Windows compatibility, stderr output separation, and security hardening.
